chunks.text:
Software Requirements Specification
Standalone Material Code Request
17th Sep 2026

chunks.title: Purpose
chunks.heading: Purpose
chunks.text:
The purpose of this enhancement is to allow users to request a new Material Code directly without requiring a Techpack or BOM. Users can select a Category, provide the required details, and submit the request to Sourcing for review and material creation.
The existing BOM-linked Material Creation Request process will remain unchanged.

chunks.title: Functional Flow (User Side)
chunks.heading: Functional Flow (User Side)
chunks.text:
A new screen will be provided to the user to create a Standalone Material Creation Request. From this screen, the user will be able to initiate a request for creating a new Material Code without requiring a Techpack or BOM.
Step 1: User will click on “Standalone Material Request” Option as shown above.
Path : Catalog >> Industrial Engineering >> Article Request >> Standalone Material Request
Step 2: After clicking on the Standalone Material Request a new screen opens where the user can see the list of all Material Requests sent by them.
Material Code Request – List
This screen displays the list of all Material Code Requests created in the system. It allows users to track the current status and progress of each request.
The following details are displayed for each request:
• Material Code Request: Unique request number generated by the system.
• Status: Displays the current status of the request, such as Pending, Approved, or Rejected.
• Article Code: Displays the generated Article/Material Code once the request is approved.
• Pending With: Displays the user with whom the request is currently pending for action.
• Style: Displays the Style associated with the request, if applicable.
• Buyer: Displays the Buyer details.
• Created On: Displays the date on which the Material Code Request was created.

chunks.title: Functional Flow (User Side)
chunks.heading: Functional Flow (User Side)
chunks.text:
• Remarks: Displays additional information, approval details, or the rejection reason.
Users can use the search and filter options available in the grid to find specific Material Code Requests.
The New button allows the user to create a new Standalone Material Creation Request.
Step 3: After clicking on the New button, a new screen will open named Standalone Material Code Request.
The screen will display a grid where the user can add one or more material requests. For each request, the user will be able to provide the required material details, including:
• Material Type
• Product Category
• Subcategory
• Article Description
• Buyer
• Style
• Remarks
• User
• Attachment – User can attach PDF, Image or Document.
The Product Category and Subcategory fields will allow the user to select the applicable category and subcategory details for the material request.
Users can use the Add option to add a new material request row and the Delete option to remove selected request rows.
Once all required details are provided, the user can select the appropriate user and click Send to submit the Standalone Material Creation Request for further processing.
The screen also supports selection of multiple records using checkboxes and provides pagination for managing multiple material creation requests.

chunks.title: Functional Flow (Approver’s Side)
chunks.heading: Functional Flow (Approver’s Side)
chunks.text:
Once the user submits a Standalone Material Creation Request, the request will be sent to the respective approver/Sourcing user for further action.
The approver will be able to view all the details submitted in the Material Code Request, including the selected material category, applicable material details, comments, and attachments.
Step 1: Identify Request Source
In the Material Code Request List screen, the approver will be able to identify the source from which the Material Code Request was created. The request can be identified as either:
• BOM-linked Material Code Request, or
• Standalone Material Creation Request
This will help the approver understand whether the request was initiated from an existing BOM or created directly through the Standalone Material Creation Request functionality.
Here, as shown in the above screen, the approver will be able to identify the source of the Material Code Request. If the request is created from a BOM, BOM will be displayed as the request source. If the request is created through the Standalone Material Creation Request screen, Without BOM will be displayed.
Step 2: View Attachment

chunks.title: Functional Flow (Approver’s Side)
chunks.heading: Functional Flow (Approver’s Side)
chunks.text:
After opening the Material Code Request, the approver will be able to view and access any attachment uploaded by the user while creating the request. The approver can review the attached document or file before proceeding with the Material/Article creation process.
Here you can clearly see that Attachment will be accessed by Approver as well for better visbility.
Note: The workflow will remain the same as the existing Material Code Request process. However, for a Standalone Material Creation Request, when the approver clicks Create New Article, the system will automatically select and populate the Material Type, Product Group and Sub Category based on the details available in the Material Code Request.
Since these details are already provided by the requester while creating and submitting the request, the approver will not be required to select them again.

Here, the Material Type, Product Group, and Sub Category are auto-populated based on the sender's selection. The approver does not need to select these fields again.
Additional Point: When the actual material code is mapped to generic article, the consumption UOM in BOM line has to be fetched from UOM defined in the respective article master.
